In Salento, a stop at a viewpoint overlooking the valley is planned.

On arrival in Cocora Valley, guests are welcomed with a canelazo drink and introduced to a local eco-guide. The walk then begins along an ecological trail through cloud forest to the wax palms, a national symbol of Colombia and the tallest palms in the world.

A separate part of the program is devoted to the history and traditions associated with the Quindío wax palm. The excursion includes a palm-planting ceremony as a way to learn about local culture and efforts to conserve the species.

After the valley, the route continues to Salento. Here you will walk along colonial streets, discover local workshops and crafts, and enjoy the views from the Cocora viewpoint.

Hotel pickup is scheduled for 9:00.

Accompanied by a private guide, you will travel toward the shores of the immense bay, passing along scenic streets and shaded avenues before arriving in Pelourinho, a historic district listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the largest and best-preserved ensembles of colonial architecture in South America.

Leaving your vehicle in Municipal Square beside the imposing Lacerda Elevator, you can enjoy magnificent views over the bay and Lower Town.

The walk then continues along the narrow, lively streets of the historic quarter, surrounded by brightly colored buildings. Here you can experience the atmosphere of old Salvador, with its music, color and rich cultural heritage.

You will visit São Francisco Church, famous for its lavish Baroque interior richly decorated with gilding. The excursion continues to Pelourinho Square, considered the heart of Salvador's old town.

As you explore the city, you will also experience the distinctive local traditions, from the energetic movements of capoeira to the famous acarajé dish and the ancient spiritual traditions of Candomblé.

From Santa Cruz, you will travel approximately 120 km to Samaipata, a colonial town in the Andean foothills at an altitude of about 1,650 meters. Along the way, you can admire green valleys, hills and mountain ranges.

The main part of the excursion is El Fuerte de Samaipata, at an altitude of around 1,950 meters, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The complex was a ceremonial and administrative center and the last stronghold of the Inca Empire before the Spanish conquest. The carved rock features two massive parallel grooves, zoomorphic figures, water channels, stairways and niches associated with religious rituals.

After visiting El Fuerte, you will return to Samaipata for a traditional Bolivian lunch made with local ingredients before traveling back to Santa Cruz.

In Lima's historic center, we will visit [Main Square](/peru/place/plaza-mayor-lima/) with [Lima Cathedral](/peru/place/lima-cathedral/) and [San Francisco Monastery](/peru/place/san-francisco-monastery-lima/). Along the way, you will see colonial buildings with traditional wooden balconies.

The tour then continues through the city's residential districts. In [San Isidro](/peru/place/san-isidro-lima/), you will see an olive grove, the Country Club and a golf course.

In [Miraflores](/peru/place/miraflores-lima/), the route passes through Central Park, City Hall and the main shopping streets, including Larco Avenue. A return to the hotel is arranged after the excursion.
